answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because bridge only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. In practice vine is enforced by the ledger itself: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any comet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
